questions.question: If the perimeter of one face of a cube is 48 cm, then its volume is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **cube**, all faces are **squares**.

**Side (a)** = **Perimeter** ÷ 4 = 48 ÷ 4 = 12 cm

**Volume** = (Side)³ = 12³

**Volume** = 1728 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 1728 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Perimeter** of one face = 48 cm

**Formula Used:**

**Perimeter** of a square face = 4 × a

**Volume** of a cube = a³

where **'a'** is the side of the **cube**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/684faf62b3125c5258419ebf9f2be8d7e44ba2f9006d04a15a65ff4fc4ee6a05.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 4 × a = 48

⇒ a = 48 ÷ 4

⇒ a = 12 cm

Now, calculate the **Volume**:

⇒ **Volume** = a × a × a

⇒ **Volume** = 12 × 12 × 12

⇒ **Volume** = 1728 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 1728 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of Cube

The total area of all six faces of the **cube** is given by the formula TSA = 6a².

Lateral Surface Area (LSA)

The area of the four vertical faces (excluding top and bottom) is LSA = 4a².

Diagonal of a Cube

The longest distance between two opposite corners of a **cube** is d = a√3.

Face Diagonal

The diagonal of a single square face of the **cube** is given by dfₐ꜀ₑ = a√2.</p

questions.question: The square of the length of a space diagonal of a closed cube is 2175 cm². What is the total surface area (in cm²) of the cube?

**Total Surface Area** (TSA) of a cube = 6a².

Relation: TSA = 2 × (Square of **Space Diagonal**).

TSA = 2 × 2175 = 4350 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 4350 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Square of the length of the **space diagonal** = 2175 cm².

Formula used: **Space Diagonal** (d) = a√3 | **Total Surface Area** = 6a².

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/671a6ab1dbb4c460569c48ad58990b6ff63813c3419c3db12a95f425d74359f4.png] 

⇒ d² = (a√3)² = 3a²

⇒ 3a² = 2175 cm²

⇒ a² = 2175 ÷ 3 = 725 cm²

⇒ **Total Surface Area** = 6a²

⇒ Total Surface Area = 6 × 725 = 4350 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 4350 cm².**

Face Diagonal of a Cube

The length of the diagonal of any one face is given by a√2, where 'a' is the side of the cube.

Volume of a Cube

The total space occupied by the cube is Volume (V) = a³ cubic units.

Lateral Surface Area

The area of the four vertical faces of the cube is Lateral Surface Area (LSA) = 4a² sq. units.</p

questions.question: Water flows into a tank having the dimensions of its base given as 200 m × 150 m through a rectangular pipe having dimensions given as 1.5 m × 1.25 m @ 20 kmph. In what time (in minutes) will the water rise by 2 meters?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Time** = (Volume of tank) ÷ (Area of pipe cross-section × Speed of flow)

Total **Volume** required = 200 × 150 × 2 = 60,000 m³

**Flow rate** per hour = 1.5 × 1.25 × 20,000 = 37,500 m³/hr

Time (in hours) = 60,000 ÷ 37,500 = 1.6 hours

Time (in min) = 1.6 × 60 = 96 min

**∴ The correct answer is 96 min.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Tank** dimensions: Length = 200 m, Breadth = 150 m, Height of water rise = 2 m

**Pipe** dimensions: Width = 1.5 m, Depth = 1.25 m

**Speed** of water = 20 kmph = 20,000 m/hr

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/68423fea2d60f1d53f008bfe66ab21e934b28b4995f99978e6dfb7b24860fc00.png] 

⇒ Volume of water required = Length × Breadth × Height

⇒ Volume = 200 × 150 × 2 = 60,000 m³

⇒ Area of **cross-section** of pipe = 1.5 × 1.25 = 1.875 m²

⇒ Speed of water in m/min = (20 × 1000) ÷ 60 = 1000 ÷ 3 m/min

⇒ Volume of water flowing per minute = Area × Speed

⇒ Flow rate = 1.875 × (1000 ÷ 3) = 625 m³/min

⇒ Time taken = Total Volume ÷ Flow rate per minute

⇒ Time = 60,000 ÷ 625 = 96 min

**∴ The correct answer is 96 min.**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of Cuboid

The volume of a rectangular tank is given by Length × Breadth × Height (L × B × H).

Rate of Flow

The amount of water flowing through a pipe per unit time is Area of cross-section × Velocity of flow.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/min, multiply by (1000 ÷ 60) or 50 ÷ 3.</p

questions.question: Find the number of bricks, each measuring 24 cm × 12 cm × 8 cm, required to construct a wall 24 m long, 8m high and 60 cm thick if 10% of the wall is filled with mortar?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Number of bricks = (90% of **Wall Volume**) ÷ (**Brick Volume**)

Volume of wall = 2400 × 800 × 60 cm³ (Converting m to cm)

Number of bricks = (0.9 × 2400 × 800 × 60) ÷ (24 × 12 × 8)

Number of bricks = 0.9 × 100 × 100 × 5 = 45000

**∴ The correct answer is 45000 bricks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Brick dimensions: 24 cm × 12 cm × 8 cm

Wall dimensions: 24 m × 8 m × 60 cm

Mortar usage: 10% of **wall volume**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f75e7e843c07535710f625cc233d7f661b322ff4d91d61d29975b61d3fcd564c.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Volume of Cuboid = length × breadth × height

Available volume for bricks = Total wall volume − Mortar volume

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total **Wall Volume** = 2400 × 800 × 60 cm³ = 115,200,000 cm³

⇒ **Mortar Volume** = 10% of 115,200,000 = 11,520,000 cm³

⇒ Volume occupied by **bricks** = 115,200,000 − 11,520,000 = 103,680,000 cm³

⇒ Volume of one **brick** = 24 × 12 × 8 = 2304 cm³

⇒ Total **number of bricks** = 103,680,000 ÷ 2304

⇒ Total number of bricks = 45000

**∴ The correct answer is 45000 bricks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cuboid

The volume of a cuboid is calculated by multiplying its three dimensions: Volume = Length × Width × Height.

Unit Conversion

Always ensure all measurements are in the same unit before calculation. 1 meter = 100 centimeters; 1 m³ = 1,000,000 cm³.

Percentage Deduction

If x% of the space is taken by another material, the remaining (100 − x)% is the effective volume available for the primary objects.</p

questions.question: The sum of the length, the breadth and the height of a cuboid is 38 cm and the length of its diagonal is 22 cm. Find the total surface area of the cuboid.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct algebraic identity: (l + b + h)² = (l² + b² + h²) + 2(lb + bh + hl)

Here, (l² + b² + h²) = Diagonal² and 2(lb + bh + hl) = **Total Surface Area** (TSA).

Shortcut formula: **TSA** = (Sum of dimensions)² − (Diagonal)²

⇒ **TSA** = 38² − 22² = 1444 − 484 = 960 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 960 cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of **length**, **breadth**, and **height** (l + b + h) = 38 cm

Length of the **diagonal** (d) = 22 cm

**Formula Used:**

1. **Diagonal of a cuboid** = √(l² + b² + h²)

2. **Total Surface Area (TSA)** = 2(lb + bh + hl)

3. Algebraic identity: (l + b + h)² = l² + b² + h² + 2(lb + bh + hl)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/301db4b1b6ed1db5d9f4f295cf5a8fbf56cdd5c1197c5ea5afdc2a0fc2875790.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Diagonal = √(l² + b² + h²) = 22

⇒ Squaring both sides: l² + b² + h² = 22² = 484

⇒ We know (l + b + h) = 38

⇒ Squaring both sides: (l + b + h)² = 38²

⇒ l² + b² + h² + 2(lb + bh + hl) = 1444

⇒ 484 + **TSA** = 1444

⇒ **TSA** = 1444 − 484

⇒ **TSA** = 960 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 960 cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cuboid

The space occupied by a cuboid is given by the product of its three dimensions: **Volume** = l × b × h.

Lateral Surface Area (LSA)

The area of the four side walls of the cuboid (excluding top and bottom) is **LSA** = 2h(l + b).

Special Case: Cube

When l = b = h = a, the cuboid becomes a cube. **Diagonal** = a√3, **TSA** = 6a², and **Volume** = a³.</p

questions.question: Given that one cubic cm of marble weighs 25 gms, the weight of a cuboidal marble block 28 cm in width and 5 cm thick is 112 kg. The length of the block is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Weight in grams = 112 × 1000 = 112,000 g

Weight = Length × Width × Thickness × Density

112,000 = Length × 28 × 5 × 25

112,000 = Length × 3,500

Length = 112,000 ÷ 3,500 = 1120 ÷ 35 = 32 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 32 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Weight of 1 cm³ marble = 25 g

Total weight of **cuboidal marble block** = 112 kg

**Width** of the block = 28 cm

**Thickness** of the block = 5 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cuboid = Length × Width × Thickness

Mass = Volume × Density

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c1ac1dc0864b658c24d71c3fff9854e3750722965a140658f903871660a50630.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Weight in grams = 112 × 1000 = 112,000 g

⇒ Total **Volume** of the block = Total Weight ÷ Density per cm³

⇒ Total Volume = 112,000 ÷ 25 = 4,480 cm³

⇒ Volume = Length × Width × Thickness

⇒ 4,480 = Length × 28 × 5

⇒ 4,480 = Length × 140

⇒ **Length** = 4,480 ÷ 140

⇒ Length = 32 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 32 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cuboid

The amount of space occupied by a three-dimensional cuboid is calculated as Volume = Length × Breadth × Height.

Relation between Mass, Density and Volume

Mass is the product of the volume of the object and its density (Mass = Volume × Density). Ensure units are consistent (e.g., g and cm³).

Unit Conversion

To convert kilograms to grams, multiply by 1000 (1 kg = 1000 g). This is essential when the density is given in g/cm³.</p

questions.question: The volume of a wall that is 5 times as high as it is broad and 8 times as long as it is high is 12.8 cubic meters. Find the breadth of the wall.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Breadth** : **Height** : **Length** = 1 : 5 : (5 × 8) = 1 : 5 : 40.

Product of ratios = 1 × 5 × 40 = 200 units³.

200 units³ = 12.8 m³ ⇒ 1 unit³ = 0.064 m³.

1 unit = ³√0.064 = 0.4 m.

**Breadth** = 0.4 × 100 cm = 40 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Volume** of the wall = 12.8 m³

**Height (h)** = 5 × **Breadth (b)**

**Length (l)** = 8 × **Height (h)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3b4f2acd0d014150f6750ca8b3d7c4b099d03151689fae9499927d78e2570d8c.png] 

**Formula Used:**

**Volume** of a **Cuboid** (Wall) = Length × Breadth × Height

**Calculations:**

Let the **Breadth** of the wall be b m.

⇒ Height (h) = 5b

⇒ Length (l) = 8 × (5b) = 40b

⇒ Volume = l × b × h

⇒ 12.8 = (40b) × (b) × (5b)

⇒ 12.8 = 200b³

⇒ b³ = 12.8 ÷ 200

⇒ b³ = 0.064

⇒ b = ³√0.064 = 0.4 m

Converting into centimeters:

⇒ Breadth = 0.4 × 100 = 40 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 40 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume and Surface Area of Cuboid

For a cuboid of dimensions l, b, and h, the **Total Surface Area (TSA)** is given by 2(lb + bh + hl) and the **Volume** is l × b × h.

Diagonal of a Cuboid

The length of the longest rod that can be placed inside a cuboid is its **Diagonal**, calculated as √(l² + b² + h²).

Unit Conversion

To convert **meters** to **centimeters**, multiply by 100 (1 m = 100 cm). For volume, 1 m³ = 1,000,000 cm³.</p

questions.question: Sameer has a solid metal ball having a diameter of 6 cm. He melts it and uses the material for making a solid cylinder. If the diameter of the base of the cylinder is same as that of the ball, what would the height of the cylinder be?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a **sphere** is melted into a **cylinder** of the same **radius** (r), their volumes are equal.

(4/3) × π × r³ = π × r² × h

This simplifies to: **h = (4/3) × r**

Given **diameter** = 6 cm ⇒ **radius** (r) = 3 cm.

Height (h) = (4/3) × 3 = 4 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Diameter of the **metal ball** (sphere) = 6 cm

Diameter of the **cylinder base** = 6 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of **Sphere** = (4/3) π r³

Volume of **Cylinder** = π r² h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/acf283fd5b556c7022c0c85d791928b3ee2504cc280b095a770783d6a51275f7.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Radius of sphere (r) = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm

⇒ Radius of cylinder base (R) = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm

⇒ Volume of Sphere = (4 ÷ 3) × π × (3)³

⇒ Volume of Sphere = (4 ÷ 3) × π × 27 = 36π cm³

⇒ Volume of Cylinder = π × (3)² × h = 9πh

⇒ Since Volume of Sphere = Volume of Cylinder:

⇒ 36π = 9πh

⇒ h = 36 ÷ 9

⇒ h = 4 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 4 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume Conservation

When a solid object is **melted** and **recast** into another shape, the **total volume** remains the same, provided there is no wastage of material.

Sphere Formulas

Volume = (4/3)πr³ | Total Surface Area = 4πr².

Cylinder Formulas

Volume = πr²h | Curved Surface Area = 2πrh | Total Surface Area = 2πr(r + h).

Hemisphere Formulas

Volume = (2/3)πr³ | Curved Surface Area = 2πr² | Total Surface Area = 3πr².</p

questions.question: Find the total surface area of a cylinder whose radius of base is 7 cm and height is 12 cm.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Total Surface Area (TSA)** of a cylinder = **2πr(r + h)**

Given: **r = 7 cm** and **h = 12 cm**

TSA = 2 × π × 7 × (7 + 12) = 14 × 19 × π

Calculation: 14 × 19 = **266**

**∴ The correct answer is 266 π cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Radius (r)** of the base = 7 cm

**Height (h)** of the cylinder = 12 cm

**Formula Used:**

Total Surface Area (TSA) = **Curved Surface Area + 2 × Base Area**

TSA = 2πrh + 2πr² = **2πr(r + h)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f6d2be3944036e7037869cbdc4cf64d0da8e595b737b2a7186ccb5c8d0b43dd9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ TSA = 2 × π × 7 × (7 + 12)

⇒ TSA = 14 × π × (19)

⇒ TSA = (14 × 19) π

⇒ TSA = 266 π cm²

The calculation shows that the total surface area is 266 π cm², which corresponds to **Option (2)**.

**∴ The correct answer is 266 π cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

The area of the side surface of the cylinder excluding the top and bottom bases is given by 2πrh.

Volume of Cylinder

The total space occupied by the cylinder is calculated using the formula Volume = πr²h.

Base Area

The area of each circular base is πr². A cylinder has two such identical bases.

Lateral Surface Area

For a cylinder, the lateral surface area is the same as the curved surface area (CSA).</p

questions.question: The radius of a cylinder is 5 cm more than its height. If the curved surface area of the cylinder is 792 cm², then the volume of the cylinder (in cm³), is ________. [Use pi = (22)/(7) ]
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2 × π × r × h = 792 ⇒ π × r × h = 396

Volume of a cylinder is π × r² × h = (π × r × h) × r = 396 × r

Since 2 × (22/7) × r × (r − 5) = 792 ⇒ r × (r − 5) = 126

By simple observation, 14 × (14 − 5) = 126, so the radius r = 14 cm

Volume = 396 × 14 = 5544 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 5544 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of cylinder (r) = height (h) + 5

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 792 cm²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/90e5452c5c92732388895bd613d39b0b616a48b1d86763138ca5097202c8bd9a.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2 × π × r × h

Volume of cylinder = π × r² × h

**Calculation:**

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × (h + 5) × h = 792

⇒ (44/7) × (h² + 5h) = 792

⇒ h² + 5h = 792 × 7 ÷ 44

⇒ h² + 5h = 18 × 7

⇒ h² + 5h − 126 = 0

⇒ h² + 14h − 9h − 126 = 0

⇒ h(h + 14) − 9(h + 14) = 0

⇒ (h − 9)(h + 14) = 0

⇒ h = 9 cm (since height cannot be negative)

⇒ Radius (r) = 9 + 5 = 14 cm

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × (14)² × 9

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 196 × 9 = 22 × 28 × 9

⇒ Volume = 616 × 9 = 5544 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 5544 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Cylinder

A cylinder is a 3D solid with two parallel circular bases. Total Surface Area (TSA) = CSA + 2 × Base Area = 2 × π × r × (r + h).

Volume of Related Shapes

The volume of a cone with the same base radius and height as a cylinder is exactly one-third of the cylinder's volume. Cone Volume = (1/3) × π × r² × h.

Circumference and Area of Base

The base of a cylinder is a circle. Base Area = π × r² and Base Perimeter (Circumference) = 2 × π × r. The CSA can directly be calculated as Base Perimeter × height.
</p

questions.question: The radius of the base and the height of a closed cylinder are in the ratio 1 : 3. Using π = (22/7), find its total surface area if its curved surface area is 924 m².
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **radius (r)** to **height (h)** = 1 : 3.

Direct relationship: **TSA / CSA = (r + h) / h**.

Substituting the ratios: **TSA / 924 = (1 + 3) / 3 = 4 / 3**.

**TSA** = 924 × (4 / 3) = 308 × 4 = 1232 m².

**∴ The correct answer is 1232 m².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of **radius (r)** to **height (h)** = 1 : 3

**Curved Surface Area (CSA)** = 924 m²

**Formula Used:**

CSA of **cylinder** = 2πrh

**Total Surface Area (TSA)** of **cylinder** = 2πr(h + r)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3b4afbd81ff97efc93e998570adef82ced1a192aca3b300c135ffef5b1fe1952.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let **radius (r)** = x and **height (h)** = 3x

⇒ CSA = 2 × (22/7) × x × 3x = 924

⇒ (132 / 7) × x² = 924

⇒ x² = (924 × 7) / 132

⇒ x² = 7 × 7 = 49

⇒ x = 7 m

⇒ **radius (r)** = 7 m and **height (h)** = 3 × 7 = 21 m

⇒ TSA = 2 × (22/7) × 7 × (21 + 7)

⇒ TSA = 44 × 28

⇒ TSA = 1232 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 1232 m².**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cylinder

The **volume** represents the capacity and is calculated as V = πr²h.

Total Surface Area Components

For a **closed cylinder**, TSA = CSA + 2 × Base Area = 2πrh + 2πr².

Ratio Property

If the ratio of r:h is known, the ratio of TSA:CSA is always (r+h):h, which is independent of the actual dimensions.</p

questions.question: The volume of a cylinder is 5500 m³. Find its diameter of base if the height of the cylinder is 70 m. [Use pi = (22)/(7)]

questions.question: A solid metallic sphere of radius 12 cm is melted and recast in the form of small spheres of radius 2 cm. How many small spheres are formed?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For melting and recasting **spheres**, the number of small spheres (n) = (R ÷ r)³.

Given **Large Radius (R)** = 12 cm and **Small Radius (r)** = 2 cm.

n = (12 ÷ 2)³ = 6³

n = 6 × 6 × 6 = 216

**∴ The correct answer is 216.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the **metallic sphere** (R) = 12 cm

Radius of each **small sphere** (r) = 2 cm

**Formula Used:**

**Volume of a sphere** = (4/3) × π × (radius)³

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7b99aea85ecfc2f47011d25ae13bf5050ec0053d07899a49134439bc3fb78dc9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total volume of material remains constant during **recasting**.

⇒ Volume of large sphere = n × Volume of one small sphere

⇒ (4/3) × π × R³ = n × (4/3) × π × r³

⇒ R³ = n × r³

⇒ 12³ = n × 2³

⇒ 1728 = n × 8

⇒ n = 1728 ÷ 8

⇒ n = 216

**∴ The correct answer is 216.**

**__Additional Information__**

Conservation of Volume

When a solid object is **melted** and **recast** into new shapes, the total volume of the material remains the same, provided there is no wastage.

Sphere Properties

The **Surface Area** of a sphere is 4πr² and the **Volume** is (4/3)πr³. For a hemisphere, the volume is (2/3)πr³.

Ratio of Volumes

If the radii of two spheres are in the ratio a : b, then the ratio of their **volumes** is a³ : b³ and the ratio of their **surface areas** is a² : b².</p

questions.question: If the radius of a sphere is increased by 50%, find the increase percent in the volume.

**∴ The correct answer is 237.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/29232e2aa63d835a0b913f3366823f458c838b2fd895b0f01398fedfe039493e.png]

⇒ % Increase = [((4/3) × π × (3375000 − 1000000)) ÷ ((4/3) × π × 1000000)] × 100

⇒ % Increase = (2375000 ÷ 1000000) × 100

⇒ % Increase = 2.375 × 100 = 237.5%

Successive Percentage Rule

Sphere Properties

questions.question: If the radius of a sphere is increased by 50%, find the percent increase in the surface area.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When a dimension changes by **x%**, the area (which depends on the square of the dimension) changes by the **successive percentage** formula: **x + x + (x × x)/100**.

Given **radius** increase = 50%.

Net percentage increase in **Surface Area** = 50 + 50 + (50 × 50)/100.

Net percentage increase = 100 + 25 = 125%.

**∴ The correct answer is 125%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Increase in **radius** of the **sphere** = 50%

**Formula Used:**

Surface area (A) of a sphere = 4πr²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7c484b184b5b2c0c36c36edc577f55bb0e9c5cd2acb835a6e3ab8431678a149b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **original radius** be r.

⇒ Original **Surface Area** (A₁) = 4πr²

⇒ New radius (R) = r + 50% of r = r + 0.5r = 1.5r

⇒ New **Surface Area** (A₂) = 4πR² = 4π(1.5r)²

⇒ A₂ = 4π × 2.25r² = 2.25 × (4πr²) = 2.25A₁

⇒ Increase in area = A₂ − A₁ = 2.25A₁ − A₁ = 1.25A₁

⇒ **Percentage increase** = (Increase / Original Area) × 100

⇒ Percentage increase = (1.25A₁ / A₁) × 100 = 125%

**∴ The correct answer is 125%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume Change for Sphere

Since Volume V ∝ r³, if the radius increases by 50% (factor of 1.5), the volume increases by (1.5)³ = 3.375 times, which is a 237.5% increase.

General Area Scaling Rule

If all linear dimensions of any 3D shape change by a factor of k, then the **surface area** changes by a factor of k² and the **volume** changes by a factor of k³.

The curved surface area of a hemisphere is 2πr² and the **total surface area** is 3πr².</p

questions.question: If the radius of a sphere is increased by 2 cm, then its surface area increases by 704 cm². Using π = 22/7 \frac{22}{7} , find the radius of the sphere after the increase.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Sum of radii (R + r) = Increase in Area / (4 × π × increase in radius)

R + r = 704 / (4 × 22/7 × 2) = 704 / (176/7) = 28 cm.

Given the difference in radii (R − r) = 2 cm.

Radius after increase (R) = (Sum + Difference) / 2 = (28 + 2) / 2 = 15 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Increase in **surface area** = 704 cm²

Increase in **radius** = 2 cm

**Formula Used:**

**Surface area** of a sphere = 4πr²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bb6892dbf935cdce0643a2340a111e3143612937e981f6f185565367cff4c93b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial **radius** be r cm and the increased **radius** be R = (r + 2) cm.

⇒ 4πR² − 4πr² = 704

⇒ 4 × (22/7) × (R² − r²) = 704

⇒ (88/7) × (R − r)(R + r) = 704

⇒ (88/7) × 2 × (R + r) = 704

⇒ (176/7) × (R + r) = 704

⇒ R + r = (704 × 7) / 176

⇒ R + r = 28

⇒ (r + 2) + r = 28 ⇒ 2r = 26 ⇒ r = 13 cm

⇒ **Radius after increase** (R) = 13 + 2 = 15 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 cm.**

Volume of a Sphere

questions.question: A ball of radius 10 cm is taken and a cylindrical hole of radius 1 cm is drilled through the centre. Which of the options listed below is the closest in value to the ratio of the total surface area of the hollowed out ball to the surface area of the original ball?

⇒ Surface area of original ball = 4 × π × 10² = 400π cm²

⇒ Ratio ≈ (33 × 3.3166) ÷ 100 = 109.4478 ÷ 100 = 1.094478

⇒ Checking Option 1: 219 ÷ 200 = 1.095

**∴ The correct answer is 219/200.**

The ratio of their total surface areas.

TSA₁ / TSA₂ = (3 / 4)²

**Therefore, the ratio of their total surface areas is 9 : 16.**
